item: 6.5 Mention from the IDE — a `__mention` host frame inserts @-mention tokens into the composer at the caret (2026-09-04)
branch: the Project-view / editor context-menu action (MentionAction.kt) sends {type:'__mention', items:[relative paths]}; the webview inserts `@path ` per item at the caret — a separating space before when the caret follows a non-space character, one trailing space after each token — leaves the caret after the insertion, and focuses the composer
provenance: __mention is OUR OWN host frame (ChatPanel.insertMentions), never on the CLI wire — renderer-vs-frame self-consistency by construction. The Kotlin half (VIRTUAL_FILE_ARRAY → project-relative paths, directories with a trailing slash, tool-window activation) is unit-tested in MentionActionTest and hand-verified in the sandbox. Modelled on VS Code's `claude-vscode.insertAtMention` (Alt+K) generalised to a multi-select context menu, per the user's request 2026-09-04. Negative control: on the pre-6.5 build the frame is unknown to the event switch and the composer stays untouched — every value assert fails.

steps.note: A: two items appended to a non-empty composer whose caret sits at its end (no trailing space) → one separating space, then `@a @b/ `; B: empty composer → `@x `; C: caret in the middle of `abcd` → tokens spliced with a space on both sides
steps.setup: window.__mn75 = (function () { window.onClaudeEvent(JSON.stringify({type:'__clear'})); const input = document.getElementById('input'); input.value = 'look at'; input.setSelectionRange(input.value.length, input.value.length); window.onClaudeEvent(JSON.stringify({type:'__mention', items:['src/components/App.tsx', 'docs/']})); const a = { value: input.value, caret: input.selectionStart, focused: document.activeElement === input }; input.value = ''; input.setSelectionRange(0, 0); window.onClaudeEvent(JSON.stringify({type:'__mention', items:['x.js']})); const b = { value: input.value, caret: input.selectionStart }; input.value = 'abcd'; input.setSelectionRange(2, 2); window.onClaudeEvent(JSON.stringify({type:'__mention', items:['x.js']})); const c = { value: input.value, caret: input.selectionStart }; input.value = ''; return { a: a, b: b, c: c }; })();

expect.why: DISCRIMINATING: both items become `@path ` tokens, separated from the existing text by exactly one space (pre-fix: 'look at')
DISCRIMINATING: the caret lands after the insertion, ready to keep typing
GUARD: the composer takes focus so the next keystroke goes to it
DISCRIMINATING: an empty composer gets no leading space
DISCRIMINATING: a mid-word caret gets a space on both sides, so the token never fuses with its neighbours
GUARD: caret sits after the token's trailing space, before the remaining text
